title: The Zojila Tunnel Just Broke Through. The World's Longest High-Altitude Road Tunnel Is Six Months Ahead of Schedule.
excerpt: A controlled blast connected Kashmir and Ladakh through 13 kilometres of Himalayan rock at 11,578 feet. The tunnel will end five months of winter isolation when it opens in 2028.
body:
A controlled blast on June 9 punched through the last 2.5 metres of rock inside the Zojila Tunnel, connecting its east and west portals and completing the excavation of what will be the world's longest single-tube, bi-directional road tunnel at an altitude above 11,500 feet. The breakthrough came six months ahead of schedule.

Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari triggered the blast remotely from the tunnel's East Portal at Minimarg in Ladakh's Kargil district. Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stood alongside him. Gadkari called it "a golden day" in India's infrastructure history.

"This is not just a tunnel but a lifeline," Gadkari said. He recalled visiting Ladakh during his tenure as BJP president, when residents told him that road connectivity shut down for nearly six months every winter. "People told me everything remains closed for six months. It pained me."

## The Numbers

The Zojila Tunnel stretches 13.15 kilometres from Baltal in Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir to Minimarg in the Drass sector of Ladakh. It sits on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway and is supported by an 18.5-kilometre approach road that includes five bridges and two snow tunnels.

The excavation was completed from an equidistant point of 6.5 kilometres, with crews drilling simultaneously from both portals. The project was built by MEIL (Megha Engineering and Infrastructure Limited) under the National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation at a cost of approximately Rs 6,500-7,000 crore — significantly below the original tender of Rs 12,000 crore, Gadkari noted.

About 80 per cent of the workers on the project were locals from the region — a detail Gadkari highlighted as the tunnel was built in harsh sub-zero conditions at one of the most challenging high-altitude construction sites in the world.

## What It Changes

The Zojila Pass, at 11,578 feet, has been one of India's most treacherous mountain corridors. Every winter, heavy snowfall and avalanches cut the pass off for roughly five months, severing the only land connection between the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh. During those months, residents of Leh and surrounding areas are forced to fly — at peak-season costs exceeding Rs 40,000 for a one-way ticket.

When operational, the tunnel will compress the 40-kilometre journey from Baltal to Minimarg into 13 kilometres. Travel time will drop from roughly 90 minutes to 15 minutes. More critically, it will remain open year-round, ending the seasonal isolation that has defined life in Ladakh for generations.

The tunnel is part of a wider infrastructure push in the region. The government is building 19 tunnels across Jammu, Kashmir, and Ladakh at a combined cost of about Rs 25,000 crore. The Zojila Tunnel is the centrepiece — the longest and most strategically significant of the lot.

## Strategic and Tourism Implications

The tunnel carries obvious defence significance. Ladakh shares borders with both China and Pakistan, and the Kargil sector — where the tunnel's eastern portal sits — was the site of the 1999 war. Year-round road access to the region changes the logistics calculus for the Indian military, which has maintained a heavy presence in Ladakh since the 2020 standoff with China.

For tourists and the diaspora, the implications are equally tangible. Ladakh has become one of India's most sought-after travel destinations, but the seasonal road closure compresses the visiting window into roughly five months. NRIs planning trips home often find that the Manali-Leh and Srinagar-Leh highways are passable only from late May to October. The Zojila Tunnel, once operational, would extend road access through the winter months for the first time.

## What Remains

The breakthrough marks the completion of excavation — not the end of construction. Civil finishing work, electrical systems, ventilation, and safety infrastructure will continue for another 18 to 20 months. Officials said the tunnel is likely to open to the public in February 2028.

India's tunnel-building ambitions have accelerated under the current government. The Atal Tunnel in Rohtang, completed in 2020, provided year-round access to Lahaul-Spiti. The Zojila Tunnel is a generation beyond it in scale and altitude. If it opens on schedule, it will join a short list of high-altitude infrastructure projects that have reshaped connectivity in some of the world's most forbidding terrain.
